# Environment

<!-- Generated by pnpm env:sync from scripts/sync-env-example.ts. -->

## Validation vs loading

Environment schemas validate process variables; they never load files. Process
entrypoints load the root `.env` before importing modules that validate it.
`packages/db/prisma.config.ts` loads dotenv directly because image builds run it
before workspace source is copied.

**First-party entrypoints that must load the root `.env`** (checklist when adding a new script that imports `@cockpit-chess/env/*` or a package that does — auth, db, i18n-translate, queue, mailer, …):

| Entrypoint | Mode | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `apps/server/src/bootstrap.ts` | wrapper | The **built** Hono entry (`dist/index.mjs`); loads env before runtime imports |
| `apps/worker/src/bootstrap.ts` | wrapper | The **built** BullMQ worker entry, same reason |
| `apps/server/src/index.ts` | side effect | Hono process under `tsx` (`pnpm dev`), where plain ESM order applies |
| `apps/worker/src/index.ts` | side effect | BullMQ worker under `tsx`, same reason |
| `scripts/doctor.ts` | side effect | `pnpm doctor` |
| `scripts/translate-locale-bundles.ts` | side effect | `pnpm i18n:translate` → `@cockpit-chess/i18n-translate` → `@cockpit-chess/env/shared` |
| `apps/web/vite.config.ts` | `loadRootDotenv()` | Config-time only — TanStack Start server functions during `vite dev` run in the Vite process, not `apps/server`. **Not** in the client/SSR output graph. Uses parsed root values for config-time defaults. |

Add variables to `packages/env/src/vars/*.ts` and `scripts/lib/env-manifest.ts`,
then run `pnpm env:sync`. The examples are generated; production secrets belong
in deployment settings, and disposable local credentials belong in ignored env files.

## Migration and backup inputs

`MIGRATE_ON_START` is shell-only: the server defaults to true, while workers
wait up to 300 seconds for committed migrations and register before serving.
With a separate one-shot `migrate` job, set it false on both runtime roles.
`COCKPIT_CHESS_INSTANCE_ID` is an optional shared UUID generated fresh by the
image entrypoint and reused by admission and the host heartbeat; never set it
as operator configuration. `BUILD_VERSION` is a build argument containing the
full Git SHA; the image bakes it into a file beside the bundle.

`BACKUP_ENABLED=true` enables freshness monitoring only. It never suppresses
manual, pre-migrate, pre-drop, restore or daily writing when false. Daily
writing starts off: enable exactly one `BACKUP_SCHEDULE=daily` service, with
`BACKUP_HOUR_UTC=3` (0–23) and `BACKUP_KEEP=14` (1–365). Pre-migrate snapshots
keep five; the migration runner explicitly keeps five for pre-drop snapshots.
Other direct manual/pre-restore labels default to unbounded local retention.
S3 expiration belongs to the bucket lifecycle policy.

Fresh installs need no snapshot. Existing databases without a destination
warn; failures of configured backups block migration. Explicit `--required`
and replacement-restore snapshot requirements still apply. Use a distinct
`BACKUP_S3_PREFIX` per deployment; generated Compose includes environment and
host. Writer/restore credentials need GetObject, GetObjectVersion, PutObject
and AbortMultipartUpload. Monitoring uses separate ListBucket-only credentials.

`CHECK_DATABASE_URL` belongs only to disposable migration CI checks.
`DEPLOY_CHECK_URL` and optional `DEPLOY_CHECK_TIMEOUT` are repository Actions
variables for the opt-in main-branch deploy check, not app runtime inputs.
Restore uses explicit command arguments and preview/confirmation; no restore
configuration belongs on ordinary application services. See
[Schema migrations](schema-migrations.md) and [Backup and restore](backup-restore.md).

## Client IP and reverse proxies

`TRUST_PROXY_HOPS` is the exact number of trusted reverse proxies between the
client and the server. Anonymous rate limits key on the
address the outermost counted proxy appended to `X-Forwarded-For`. The
default `0` keys on the TCP socket peer and ignores `X-Forwarded-For`, which
is correct when the server port is reached directly. Behind a proxy with `0`,
every client shares the proxy's single rate-limit bucket; generated Dokploy
configuration sets `1` for Traefik. A short chain or a malformed entry falls
back to the socket peer, never to a client-supplied entry. See
[Deployment: client IP and reverse proxies](deployment.md#client-ip-and-reverse-proxies).
